subject: Mathematics
grader_notes: Round 2 retrofit clears all three previously blocking categories. (1) PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH now Level 4: expanded_walkthrough.rationale explicitly names the research frame ('multiplication-division separation … Carpenter, Fennema & Franke 1996 CGI; Anghileri 2001'), and recovery_moves are diagnostic-branched into three concrete decision points (DIAGNOSTIC A child recites multiplication but blanks on division → drill inverse-fact + array; DIAGNOSTIC B child skip-counts but stalls beyond 10× → chunking move; DIAGNOSTIC C child computes but cannot articulate → sentence-frame scaffold). A substitute teacher can act on each branch. (2) INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE now Level 4: action.differentiation.for_movement_learners explicitly adds a NO-PAPER voice/body alternative — 'children skip-count by 2s/5s/10s using fingers + claps. Body becomes the multiplication tool' — making the lesson runnable on a no-prep day with zero materials. Optional puppet still flagged with substitutes. (3) MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY now Level 4: action.steps adds a STRATEGY COMPARE beat (Step 6) where two pairs share toolkit approaches (skip-count vs known-fact recall vs array drawing) and the class compares which is fastest for 6×5, with explicit citation to Carpenter, Fennema & Franke (1996) CGI on derived facts. This satisfies the invent-and-compare requirement for L4. (4) CLARITY_VOICE remains Level 4: Maya's quotable refrain 'Skip-count UP, multiplication’s the SUM!' bookends the lesson (hook → exit_routine 3x) and joins the existing 'if you know ONE, you know FOUR' fact-family hook. (5) ALIGNMENT remains Level 4: B2.2 and B2.1 both anchored with named activities; expanded_walkthrough cross-references neighbouring days ('Yesterday Tony's regrouping … Lesson 3 to 10×10; Lesson 4 fractions; Lesson 5 ratios'). (6) LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY remains Level 4: worksheet Part 3 deliberately reverses direction (division → related multiplication) as a transfer task, and the doubles edge case (T4: 5,5,25 → only 3 facts) mirrors the lesson's common_misconceptions. PASS.
